competences: The learner identifies rights and responsibilities studied under rights of district residents — part b.
The learner describes duties that protect the rights of others in the district.
languageCompetence: Read, pronounce and spell human rights, child abuse, citizen, citizenship, protection and responsibility.
objectives: By the end of the period learners should name important rights and duties of district residents.
By the end of the period learners should answer original questions on protecting rights.
priorKnowledge: Learners already know that local councils maintain peace and security and that leaders serve residents.
materials: P4 SST notes on human rights and citizenship
references: P4 Social Studies Notes for Terms 1–3

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher introduces rights of district residents — part b by asking "7. Give any one role citizens can play towards protecting the rights of other people.". They recall the learners' earlier work on district government and community responsibilities.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall local community rules and children's rights, answer the opening question and identify familiar examples.

steps.content: Residents must respect other people's rights. People should report human rights abuse. Children have a right to education. Children have a right to medical treatment. Children have a right to protection. Citizens should obey the laws of Uganda. Citizens should pay taxes promptly. People should help maintain law and order. Residents should care for sick people. Citizens should participate in community work. People should help maintain proper sanitation. Residents should participate in productive activities. Citizenship means legal belonging to a country.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher explains the sourced content on "Remember" and writes "Residents must respect other people's rights. People should report human rights abuse." They use the original question "8. Who is a citizen?" to check understanding and correct pupils' notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the factual points about rights and responsibilities, answer the questions and copy the notes into their exercise books.

steps.content: 7. Give any one role citizens can play towards protecting the rights of other people. | 8. Who is a citizen? | 9. Give any two ways one can become a citizen of Uganda. | 10. Mention any three responsibilities of a good citizen. | 2. Mention any four examples of human rights.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher sets the original exercise questions "7. Give any one role citizens can play towards protecting the rights of other people." and "8. Who is a citizen?". They monitor written answers and correct misconceptions using the reference materials.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer questions independently, compare their responses to the lesson points and correct any wrong answers.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher revisits the main rights and duties, evaluating understanding with "9. Give any two ways one can become a citizen of Uganda." and "10. Mention any three responsibilities of a good citizen.". They allocate the final question as revision work.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners explain an important right or responsibility, answer concluding questions and record the homework.

assessment: Assess responses to "7. Give any one role citizens can play towards protecting the rights of other people.", "8. Who is a citizen?", and "9. Give any two ways one can become a citizen of Uganda.". Mark answers using the quoted notes.
homework: Complete the original sourced question "2. Mention any four examples of human rights."
